items.title: GCash: cash-in at 7-Eleven, don't redo the bank transfer
items.detail: Say “GCash cash-in”, give your number, hand over pesos (ask the fee first; about 1% at 7-Eleven). The US bank → GCash (Meridian) screen “Your bank is processing your payment” is the first ₱3,000 still settling on the bank side (up to 3 business days). It allows one at a time, so retrying won't work before about Wed Nov 25 – Thu Nov 26.

items.title: Get used to the heat: be outside every day
items.detail: Your words: “I think my stamina is actually okay. I don't see how I'm gonna increase my stamina over a week. I've been, I was cramping a lot yesterday. If anything, I just need to get used to the heat, so I don't know if I just need to be outside every single day.” Research agrees on the direction: heat adaptation takes about 7–14 days of daily exposure, about 60–90 minutes of activity in the heat, with heart-rate gains in 3–5 days. Put salt/sodium in your drinks while adapting (sweat loses sodium). Cramping cause isn't established from this.

todos.title: Set up paying · do these once

items.title: 1. Verify GCash with your passport (5 min, approved within 24 h)
items.detail: Why it failed: GCash says “You must be a Fully Verified user to send money.” Until then you can only scan a merchant's QR Ph code. In GCash: Profile → Verify Now → scan your passport → take a selfie. You get an SMS within 24 hours. This unlocks Send Money to people (Adelmo, Mark) and bank cash-in.

items.title: 2. Make sure your card allows online and international payments
items.detail: GCash charges your linked card directly. Open your card's app and turn on online/e-commerce and international payments; turn off any travel lock. Then GCash → Profile → My Linked Accounts → Credit/Debit Cards → set it as default.

items.title: 3. Get pesos: change US cash at a money changer
items.detail: Your cheapest cash with no debit card. Go with Adelmo to a mall money changer (Czarina or Sanry's in Makati). Bring crisp, unfolded new-design $100 bills and your passport. Count the pesos at the counter. Ask for ₱20, ₱50 and ₱100 notes. Change one or two $100s at a time (about ₱6,300 each). Don't pull cash from an ATM with a credit card: that's a cash advance, about 6–8% plus interest from day one.

items.title: 4. In person: tap card or Apple Pay where there's a contactless terminal
items.detail: Works at malls, chains and nicer restaurants. At a restaurant, ask “Card or Apple Pay okay?” before ordering. Jeepneys, tricycles, small stores, markets, club courts and tips are cash only. Grab rides: in the Philippines Grab charges rides to your GrabPay balance, and your US Visa can't top that up (Grab: “This foreign card isn't supported for top-ups”). Pay rides in cash, or load GrabPay at 7-Eleven or from GCash.

items.title: 5. Online: pay with your credit card
items.detail: Card works for websites and app stores (not Grab rides, see step 4). After step 1, you can also pay any QR Ph code from GCash.

items.title: 6. Paying people back (Adelmo, Mark ₱900, PCA fees)
items.detail: Simplest: pesos in cash from step 3. After GCash is verified: Send Money to their GCash. From the US side: Wise from your bank account (about $3) to their GCash or bank. PCA fees are paid in cash at the desk in Paco: singles ₱1,200, doubles ₱900 per player.

items.title: 7. Water: buy bottled
items.detail: Drink bottled or filtered water only. Buy big bottles at 7-Eleven or a supermarket with pesos or card; take 2 L+ to the courts.

items.title: GCash runs out after 30 days
items.detail: Your GTourist account switches off 30 days after activation. Spend or cash out any balance before you leave.

items.title: PCA singles · confirm the entry by email
items.detail: Adelmo says he signed you up for singles, and you emailed PCA saying you'll play. Watch for their reply: the entry deadline is today, Sat Nov 21. Check the name, “Sy, Jerry” on the list, and whether there's a fee. If there's no reply, ask Alex or Adelmo to check in person.

items.title: Mark Ivan Malinis · doubles partner, fee
items.detail: He registered for doubles naming you and asked you to cover his fee; you said yes. PCA doubles is ₱900 per player (about $14), not $30–50. Pay him in cash when you meet, or by GCash after step 1. Nobody found results under his name: ask Adelmo or the PCA desk how he plays, and hit with him once before the event.

items.detail: Keep only useful things in the bag. Clean the room every day: it's the habit that earns the futon. Free up iPhone storage: Settings → General → iPhone Storage. Offload unused apps and delete big videos once they're backed up.

items.title: Where the Setinn brand name comes from, the maker of the National High School Senbatsu Tennis official uniform (【全国選抜高校テニス大会】公式ユニフォームを制作する『Setinn』ブランド名の由来とは！？)
items.detail: Shingo Arai put his own office inside the new Setinn flagship near Harajuku and says he is basically always there and wants people to come and meet him, so Tom can simply walk in. Why: Shingo is a former Senbatsu player and BEAMS buyer who started Setinn because tennis wear "wasn't cool at all", which is the same gap Tom's bandanas and clothing aim at. The shop visit is the easiest first meeting of the trip. Contact: Shingo Arai (Setinn director, BEAMS men's casual buyer), IG @sng1980 https://www.instagram.com/sng1980/ ; Setinn IG @setinn_official https://www.instagram.com/setinn_official/ ; Setinn Flagship Store (@setinn_flagshipstore https://www.instagram.com/setinn_flagshipstore/), 1F 3-51-10 Sendagaya, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo, 10am to 7pm, cashless only, https://setinn.jp/

items.title: Interview with Setinn director Arai at the 48th National High School Senbatsu Tennis Tournament (【第48回】『全国選抜高校テニス大会 x Setinn 新井ディレクター』インタビュー！！)
items.detail: Shingo's whole pitch is "make tennis cool again by doing the opposite of today's function-only tennis wear," and he openly wants brands to work together across company lines, which is exactly the opening for Tom. Why: It shows what Shingo cares about (style, community, bringing non-tennis people in, cross-brand collaboration) so Tom can talk his language, and it shows Setinn already does charity and tournament wear with Wilson. Contact: Shingo Arai (Setinn director, BEAMS men's casual buyer), IG @sng1980 https://www.instagram.com/sng1980/ ; Setinn IG @setinn_official https://www.instagram.com/setinn_official/ ; Setinn Flagship Store, 1F 3-51-10 Sendagaya, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo, 10am to 7pm, https://setinn.jp/

items.title: Setinn x Wilson custom racket session Vol. 1 (Setinn × Wilson | カスタムラケット セッション Vol.1)
items.detail: Setinn already has a hands-on design partnership with Wilson Japan, where its team builds custom rackets around personal themes, so Shingo is used to co-designing tennis gear with outside partners. Why: Shows how Setinn's team thinks about color and theme on tennis equipment, which gives Tom a concrete reference when he shows Shingo a bandana designed to match a racket or kit. Contact: Shingo Arai (Setinn director), IG @sng1980 https://www.instagram.com/sng1980/ ; Setinn IG @setinn_official https://www.instagram.com/setinn_official/ ; Setinn Flagship Store, 1F 3-51-10 Sendagaya, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo, https://setinn.jp/

items.title: UNDERCOVER Jun Takahashi Interview
items.detail: In the only clearly captioned talk, Jun Takahashi explains UNDERCOVER's PCM temperature-regulating fabric and says an exhibition (instead of a runway show) let him go back and deepen older functional ideas rather than chase new ones. Why: Jun is on Tom's Tokyo designer list, and this gives Tom a specific making topic (functional fabric that stores and releases body heat, revisited from a 2007 winter collection) to raise instead of a generic compliment. Most of the video is music or uncaptioned Japanese, so treat it as light background. Contact: UNDERCOVER, IG @undercover_lab https://www.instagram.com/undercover_lab/ (official account, 1.1M followers) ; https://undercoverism.com/ . No personal route for Jun was verified.

items.title: UNDERCOVER Jun Takahashi interview at The Corner
items.detail: Jun Takahashi says function and current technology must go into the clothes he wears and took Dieter Rams's "less but better" as his theme: cut out waste and do what you can. Why: Jun's push toward function, comfort and technology, with minimal waste, is the language Tom will use to describe tennis gear, so this gives him a shared design principle to raise with UNDERCOVER's team. Contact: UNDERCOVER official Instagram @undercover_lab (https://www.instagram.com/undercover_lab/, verified, 1.1M followers); written enquiries through the form at https://undercoverism.com/contact (no public press email; support Mon to Fri 10:00 to 17:00 JST); in person at UNDERCOVER AOYAMA, B1F Bleu Cinq Point A, 5-3-22 Minami-Aoyama, Minato-ku, Tokyo (men's 03 5778 4805).

items.title: UNDERCOVER A/W 1997-98 "Leaf": Behind the Scenes (TV excerpt)
items.detail: Jun Takahashi built UNDERCOVER by starting from copying, casting friends who "do what they love," and treating music as raw material, and his advice to young makers is simply that you have to do it. Why: This 1997 Japanese TV segment shows how Jun ran UNDERCOVER as a small Harajuku label with friends, shop builders and musicians, which is the closest model to Tom's own small tennis bandana and clothing line and gives him real history to open a conversation with in Tokyo. Contact: UNDERCOVER official Instagram @undercover_lab (https://www.instagram.com/undercover_lab/, verified, 1.1M followers); written enquiries through the form at https://undercoverism.com/contact (no public press email; support Mon to Fri 10:00 to 17:00 JST); in person at UNDERCOVER AOYAMA, B1F Bleu Cinq Point A, 5-3-22 Minami-Aoyama, Minato-ku, Tokyo (men's 03 5778 4805, women's 03 3407 1232).

items.title: UNDERCOVER 35th Anniversary Feature "but beautiful 4...": Behind the Scenes, 2025.1.25 to 3.4, Tokyo chapter
items.detail: Jun Takahashi's method is to take something everyone finds cute, like a teddy bear, add one "spice," then strip details until people can still recognize it, because "if people can't tell what it is, it doesn't communicate." Why: This is UNDERCOVER's own film of its Harajuku atelier and Tokyo makers finishing a Paris collection, so it shows Tom exactly how Jun's team works with craftspeople, how far ahead they finish pieces, and what they value in makers ("nothing but love"). Contact: UNDERCOVER official Instagram @undercover_lab (https://www.instagram.com/undercover_lab/, verified, 1.1M followers; also on YouTube as @undercover_lab, which posted this film); written enquiries through the form at https://undercoverism.com/contact (no public press email; support Mon to Fri 10:00 to 17:00 JST); in person at UNDERCOVER AOYAMA, B1F Bleu Cinq Point A, 5-3-22 Minami-Aoyama, Minato-ku, Tokyo (men's 03 5778 4805, women's 03 3407 1232).

items.title: UNDERCOVER Presents: Jun Takahashi and WTAPS TET in Conversation (2022)
items.detail: Once Jun Takahashi started taking menswear seriously, his goal became pieces stripped down enough to wear every day that still carry a philosophy, and he and WTAPS's Tetsu Nishiyama both trace that to how carefully 1990s Tokyo street brands chose the words on their graphics. Why: For a small brand like Tom's, this shows that Tokyo's street founders judge clothes by everyday wearability plus the wording and graphics on them, which is the angle Tom's bandanas and tees can lead with when he meets them. Contact: UNDERCOVER official Instagram @undercover_lab (https://www.instagram.com/undercover_lab/, verified, 1.1M followers); written enquiries through the form at https://undercoverism.com/contact (no public press email; support Mon to Fri 10:00 to 17:00 JST); in person at UNDERCOVER AOYAMA, B1F Bleu Cinq Point A, 5-3-22 Minami-Aoyama, Minato-ku, Tokyo (men's 03 5778 4805). For Tetsu Nishiyama's side: WTAPS official Instagram @wtaps_tokyo (https://www.instagram.com/wtaps_tokyo/, verified, 574K followers, links to www.wtaps.com).

items.title: Tiffany's Tokyo TV: Jun Takahashi (English)
items.detail: Jun Takahashi runs on Monday, Wednesday and Friday mornings to stop thinking about work, keeps "Balance & Chaos" as a motto, and says his ideas come from remixing music, art and friends inside himself. Why: Running is a sport-and-clothing habit Tom shares through tennis, so Jun's routine and his "Balance & Chaos" line give Tom a natural, non-salesy way to start a conversation about sportswear with him or his team. Contact: UNDERCOVER official Instagram @undercover_lab (https://www.instagram.com/undercover_lab/, verified, 1.1M followers); written enquiries through the form at https://undercoverism.com/contact (no public press email; support Mon to Fri 10:00 to 17:00 JST); in person at UNDERCOVER AOYAMA, B1F Bleu Cinq Point A, 5-3-22 Minami-Aoyama, Minato-ku, Tokyo (men's 03 5778 4805).

items.title: Nike x Undercover GYAKUSOU, Spring 2011: Behind the Scenes with Jun Takahashi
items.detail: For Nike GYAKUSOU, Jun Takahashi designs as a runner with no wasted detail and a slightly roomy fit for airflow and enjoyment, aiming for gear ordinary runners keep using rather than anything big. Why: GYAKUSOU is Jun's only long-running performance sportswear line, so his thinking on function, fit and everyday athletes is the closest match to Tom's tennis bandanas and clothing and the most relevant thing to ask him or his team about. Contact: UNDERCOVER official Instagram @undercover_lab (https://www.instagram.com/undercover_lab/, verified, 1.1M followers); written enquiries through the form at https://undercoverism.com/contact (no public press email; support Mon to Fri 10:00 to 17:00 JST); in person at UNDERCOVER AOYAMA, B1F Bleu Cinq Point A, 5-3-22 Minami-Aoyama, Minato-ku, Tokyo (men's 03 5778 4805).

items.title: BerBerJin web store: SHUNTA NAKAJIMA and BerBerJin pop-up "BE FREE! OUT OF CHAOS 2" exclusive items (【 ベルベルジン web store！SHUNTA NAKAJIMA アンドベルベルジンPOP UP｢BE FREE！OUT OF CHAOS 2｣限定商品！】)
items.detail: Shunta Nakajima's personal wardrobe is oversized, worn-in 1980s and 90s post-punk and shoegaze band tees, faded vintage Levi's and workwear, and old Converse, Vans and Jordans, so vintage music tees and fades are an easy, sincere opener with him. Why: Before Tom pitches anything to Nakajima, this shows his taste in detail (The Cure, Jesus and Mary Chain, Depeche Mode, My Bloody Valentine, big boxy fits, damage valued over perfection), and BerBerJin in Harajuku is a shop Tom can visit that already works with him. Contact: Shunta Nakajima via @almostblack_official (https://www.instagram.com/almostblack_official/) or @shuntanakajima (https://www.instagram.com/shuntanakajima/). For the pop-up, BerBerJin: @berberjin_harajuku (https://www.instagram.com/berberjin_harajuku/, 3-26-11 Jingumae, Shibuya, open 12:00 to 19:00) and @and_berberjin (https://www.instagram.com/and_berberjin/), all checked live 2026-11-19; web store https://webstore.berberjin.com/.

items.title: KREVA visits the ALMOSTBLACK atelier: inside the special collaboration and the deep side of making clothes (【KREVAが訪問】ブランドALMOSTBLACKのアトリエに潜入！特別コラボの裏側と服作りのディープな裏側を探る)
items.detail: Nakajima designs from concrete, physical problems a collaborator brings him (a phone pocket that doesn't hit the knee, a hat that is "shade," UV-cut fabric for Tokyo heat), so Tom should arrive with one specific functional problem his tennis bandanas solve. Why: Nakajima is a Raf Simons alumnus who says he got his job by drawing 100 sketches and phoning the studio, collects Japanese art, furniture and military/sport gear, and co-develops summer-heat functional pieces; a tennis bandana built for Tokyo heat and sweat is squarely in his language. Contact: Shunta Nakajima via the brand Instagram @almostblack_official (https://www.instagram.com/almostblack_official/) or his own @shuntanakajima (https://www.instagram.com/shuntanakajima/), both checked live 2026-11-19; site https://almostblackofficial.jp/.

items.title: TOKYO KNIT 2023 collaborating designer interview: YUKI HASHIMOTO (TOKYO KNIT 2023 コラボデザイナーYUKI HASHIMOTOインタビュー)
items.detail: Hashimoto found that old Tokyo knit and dye factories turned an iPad doodle and a shared mood into finished fabric without any technical jargon, so Tom can approach Tokyo makers with a clear picture of the finished bandana rather than a spec sheet. Why: Hashimoto is one of the Raf Simons-era Japanese designers on Tom's list, and here he walks through exactly the kind of small-run, factory-partnered textile work (custom jacquard, bleach-dyed patterns, a first-ever textile design) that Tom wants for his tennis bandanas and clothing in Tokyo. Contact: Yuki Hashimoto via the brand Instagram @_yuki_hashimoto_ (https://www.instagram.com/_yuki_hashimoto_/, checked live 2026-11-19; links to yuki-hashimoto.com). Press: Peel PR, Chihiro Kamatsuka, press@yuki-hashimoto.com (listed on the Rakuten Fashion Week Tokyo brand page, which may be dated).

items.title: Special talk show at TOKYO KNIT 2023: TENDER PERSON x YUKI HASHIMOTO (特別トークショー @TOKYO KNIT総合展2023【TENDER PERSON × YUKI HASHIMOTO】)
items.detail: Yuki Hashimoto treats Tokyo factories as partners with distinct personalities that grasp a design from a few vague words, so Tom should go in person with a clear finished image rather than a spec sheet. Why: Hashimoto (ex-Belgium, brand in Japan since 2018) explains how he works with Tokyo knit and dye factories, and TENDER PERSON's Yuto Yashige describes barging into factories and print shops each season; this is exactly the maker relationship Tom wants for small-run tennis bandanas and clothing in Tokyo. Contact: Yuki Hashimoto via the brand Instagram @_yuki_hashimoto_ (https://www.instagram.com/_yuki_hashimoto_/, checked live 2026-11-19; links to yuki-hashimoto.com). Press: Peel PR, Chihiro Kamatsuka, press@yuki-hashimoto.com (listed on the Rakuten Fashion Week Tokyo brand page, which may be dated).

items.title: TARO HORIUCHI 2015 S/S interview
items.detail: Horiuchi built his first runway show around Panamarenko, an Antwerp artist who kept hand-making flying machines that could never fly, so the "futuristic but analog, with a little sadness" idea is a natural, specific opener with him. Why: Horiuchi trained in Antwerp and now designs both th products and kolor, and this short clip shows what moves him (handmade objects, art from his Antwerp years, collaborators he admired as a student), which helps Tom open with a real making conversation rather than a pitch. Contact: Taro Horiuchi via th products on Instagram @th.products (https://www.instagram.com/th.products/, checked live 2026-11-19; bio says "by @tarohoriuchi"), or in person at the th products Sendagaya store, 2-30-28 Jingumae, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo. For kolor, where he is creative director, the brand IG is @kolorofficial (https://www.instagram.com/kolorofficial/).

items.title: Behind the scenes at a joint running-apparel exhibition, with an honest talk by the MMA, Ranor and RYOGEN directors ([VLOG] ランニングアパレルブランド合同展示会に密着。MMA、Ranor、RYOGENブランドディレクターの本音トーク！)
items.detail: Japan's indie running brands (MMA, Ranor, RYOGEN) all make in Japan, show to wholesale buyers at small joint exhibitions in Tokyo, and say a brand survives on delivering the numbers, not on taste. Why: It shows Tom how a one-person Tokyo apparel brand actually runs (B2B exhibitions four times a year, Japanese factories, short lead times, cash-flow pressure), and the directors openly want more young brands and overseas buyers to come to their shows, which is an opening for a tennis/running bandana maker. Contact: Yuichi Shibui (MMA founder), IG @shibuinsta_mania https://www.instagram.com/shibuinsta_mania/ and MMA @mountainmartialarts https://www.instagram.com/mountainmartialarts/ ; Ranor (made-in-Japan running wear), IG @ranor9378 https://www.instagram.com/ranor9378/ , www.ranor.jp ; RYOGEN, IG @ryogen.jp https://www.instagram.com/ryogen.jp/

items.title: "[INTRODUCTION] Mountain Martial Arts, obsessed with design and function. But when did it start, and who started it? The brand's origin, product details and history, introduced again ([INTRODUCTION] デザインと機能にこだわったマウンテンマーシャルアーツ。でも、いつから、誰が始めたの？ブランドスタートのきっかけから商品のこだわり、歴史まであらためてご紹介！)"
items.detail: Yuichi Shibui is a graphic designer and avid runner, not a trained clothing designer, who built a one-person, all made-in-Japan running brand by mixing vintage and street taste with top technical fabrics, which is close to what Tom is trying to do with tennis. Why: Shibui is the clearest model in Tokyo for a sport-first apparel brand run by one person with Japanese factories, and he says he got his first big collaboration (Joe Grant) because someone noticed the product on a run. Tom can open with running and his bandanas, and ask about Japanese factories, minimums and Polartec-style fabric access. Contact: Yuichi Shibui (MMA founder and director), Instagram @shibuinsta_mania https://www.instagram.com/shibuinsta_mania/ ; brand Instagram @mountainmartialarts https://www.instagram.com/mountainmartialarts/ ; web store https://store.mountainmartialarts.tokyo/

items.title: "TOKYO GUERRILLA RUN: a new running community in Tokyo, MOUNTAIN MARTIAL ARTS x Tani wa Hashiru. Why are they starting guerrilla runs in Tokyo? (【TOKYO GUERRILLA RUN /東京ゲリララン】東京に新たなランニングコミュニティ/MOUNTAIN MARTIAL ARTS ×タニは走る。/彼らはなぜ東京でゲリラランを始めるのか？！)"

Why: Tom runs, and this is a low-pressure way to spend an hour with Shibui and his running crowd before talking about bandanas or making. Watching MMA's and Shibui's Stories daily during Tom's December dates is the only way to catch one. Contact: Yuichi Shibui (MMA founder and director), Instagram @shibuinsta_mania https://www.instagram.com/shibuinsta_mania/ ; brand Instagram @mountainmartialarts https://www.instagram.com/mountainmartialarts/ (Guerrilla Runs are announced only in these accounts' Instagram Stories, which vanish after a day) ; web store https://store.mountainmartialarts.tokyo/

items.title: Shopping at Pilgrim Surf+Supply Shibuya, a grown-up shop for the city-and-nature dual life (【お買い物動画】都会と自然のデュアルライフ！！洗練されたファッション、サーフ、アウトドアが全て詰まった"ピルグリム サーフ+サプライ"で大人のお買い物！！)
items.detail: Pilgrim Surf+Supply Shibuya, run in Japan by BEAMS under Chris Gentile's New York direction, is one of the only shops in Tokyo that mixes surf gear with real clothing around a "city and nature dual life" idea, so it is a natural place to show a surf or sun bandana. Why: Pilgrim is one hop from Shingo Arai through BEAMS, and this tour shows what it stocks, how staff talk about product and which Tokyo surf people (Yuya Ofuji, the Ambient Wetsuits riders) gather around it. Tom can walk in, see where a bandana would sit on the shelf and ask staff in person. Contact: Pilgrim Surf+Supply Tokyo (BEAMS), 1F 1-14-7 Jinnan, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo, tel 03-5459-1690, open 11:00-20:00, https://pilgrimsurfsupply.jp/ ; Instagram @pilgrimsurfsupply_japan_news https://www.instagram.com/pilgrimsurfsupply_japan_news/ (product questions go to the store by phone). Host Yuya Ofuji (OVY director, Ambient Wetsuits co-founder): Instagram @yuyaofuji https://www.instagram.com/yuyaofuji/

items.title: Staying Fluid with Chris Gentile (Pilgrim Surf + Supply)
items.detail: Pilgrim's founder says the person who wins people over is "the 25-year-old asking a million questions with a smile," so Tom should walk into Pilgrim Tokyo curious and in person, not with a hard pitch. Why: Pilgrim mixes surf hard goods with clothing from small makers, its Tokyo shop is run by BEAMS (the same company as Setinn's Shingo Arai), and Chris calls Japanese retailers the best in the world, so a surf or sun bandana is a natural thing for Tom to show there. Contact: Pilgrim Surf+Supply Tokyo (run by BEAMS), 1F 1-14-7 Jinnan, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo, tel 03-5459-1690, 11:00-20:00, https://pilgrimsurfsupply.jp/ ; Japan Instagram @pilgrimsurfsupply_japan_news https://www.instagram.com/pilgrimsurfsupply_japan_news/ (its bio says product questions go to the store by phone); Chris Gentile through the New York shop, Instagram @pilgrimsurfsupply https://www.instagram.com/pilgrimsurfsupply/ (33 Grand St, Brooklyn)

items.title: "Big boys need big clothes": Sillage's loose-fit philosophy (「Big boys need big clothes.」大男孩的寬鬆主義－Sillage)
items.detail: Sillage's own site runs What We Wear, a store for small brands and artists' work, so offering Tom's bandanas for it is a more natural ask than requesting a meeting. Why: This is a fan's secondhand explainer, but it gives Tom the basics on Nicolas Yuthanan Chalmeau (Paris-raised, in Tokyo since 2017, oversized comfort, "customize your own clothes"). Sillage now has a physical store in Daikanyama, which Tom can visit. Contact: Nicolas Yuthanan Chalmeau, IG @yuthanan__ https://www.instagram.com/yuthanan__/ (www.yuthanan.com) ; Sillage IG @sillage.online https://www.instagram.com/sillage.online/ ; Sillage Store, 6-2 Sarugakucho, Shibuya, Tokyo 150-0033, 12:00 to 19:00, https://www.sillage.online/

items.title: How traditional Japanese hand-dyed towels are made
items.detail: Todaya Shoten in Ningyocho will make a fully custom chusen-dyed tenugui for anyone who orders enough, but bold shapes and 7 or 8 colours at most dye best, and fine detail gets lost. Why: This is the end-to-end process Tom would go through to have his bandana print made as Tokyo tenugui (stencil in Mie, chusen dyeing in Edogawa, finishing in Ningyocho), so he can walk in knowing the steps, the design limits and the questions to ask. Contact: Todaya Shoten (Rienzome), 2-1-11 Nihonbashi Horidomecho, Chuo-ku, Tokyo, tel 03-3661-9566; inquiry form https://www.rienzome.co.jp/inquiry/ ; custom orders https://www.rienzome.co.jp/ordermade/ (original designs from about 100 pieces, usually 3+ months after design approval, so a December order will not finish during the trip); IG @rienzome_tenugui https://www.instagram.com/rienzome_tenugui/ (does not answer DMs)

items.title: Gotta Hand it to Kamawanu! Shopping for Traditional Hand Towels in Tokyo
items.detail: Kamawanu's Harajuku shop, in the basement of the Ota Memorial Museum, shows how far a tenugui brand can push one standard 35 x 90 cm cloth with seasonal motifs, playful modern prints and licensed collaborations. Why: It is in Harajuku near the Setinn flagship and is the clearest example in Tokyo of a modern tenugui brand Tom can study for sizing, folding, display and price, and Kamawanu also takes original tenugui orders. Contact: Kamawanu Harajuku, B1 Ota Memorial Museum of Art, 1-10-10 Jingumae, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo, tel 03-3401-7957, 10:30-18:30, closed Mondays; original tenugui from 75 pieces; contact form https://kamawanu-store.jp/pages/contact ; IG @tenugui_kamawanu https://www.instagram.com/tenugui_kamawanu/

items.title: Double-sided dyeing with the traditional Tokyo Honzome (chusen) technique, Tokyo Wasarashi (Katsushika) (6 伝統的な染技法"東京本染(注染)"による「両面染色技術」[ 東京和晒株式会社（葛飾区）])
items.detail: Tokyo Wasarashi (now Tokyo Wasen) is a 1889 chusen dye works in Katsushika that runs hands-on tenugui dyeing classes with professional tools and was openly asking to collaborate with designers. Why: It is the most accessible way for Tom to touch Tokyo chusen dyeing during a two-week trip (book a class and leave with a real Tokyo-dyed sample), and a factory that has said it wants designer partners is a natural place to raise a small bandana run. Contact: Tokyo Wasen (東京和染, formerly Tokyo Wasarashi; name change notice dated 2026-10-01), 4-14-9 Tateishi, Katsushika-ku, Tokyo, tel 03-3693-3334 (weekdays 9:00-18:00), https://tenugui.co.jp/ ; IG @tokyowasen https://www.instagram.com/tokyowasen/ ; dyeing workshop booking https://souzou-kan.info/koubou/offer/ (GO TOKYO lists a 120-minute short course at 6,600 yen for 2 to 6 people)
